passages.original: plus in amore valet Mimnermi versus Homero:
passages.english: In love a verse of Mimnermus is worth more than Homer:

passages.original: tu non Antimacho, non tutior ibis Homero:
passages.english: you will go no safer than Antimachus, no safer than Homer:
passages.notes: Elliptical: the sense is that you will fare no better (be no safer from love) than Antimachus or Homer did.

passages.original: Orphea delenisse feras et concita dicunt
passages.english: They say that Orpheus soothed wild beasts and rushing
passages.notes: The sentence continues beyond this line; 'concita' (rushing, stirred up) agrees with a noun in the following line, probably rivers (flumina).
